title: Capacity Echo Replay: deterministic throughput suite for Dedicated acceptance
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement the 'Capacity Echo Replay' suite: a deterministic, tenant-aware load harness and benchmarking methodology that can reproduce customer traffic signatures against Dedicated capacity pools to provide objective throughput guarantees and a customer-facing acceptance report. The goal is to enable consistent, reproducible validation for reserved capacity contracts and to power the Dedicated onboarding checklist. This ticket covers: runner design, calibration against tenant traces, autoscaler interaction tests, SLO/SLI measurement taxonomy, and the canonical acceptance report template.
acceptance_criteria: Runner can replay a tenant workload profile with deterministic arrival patterns and KV-cache priming across GPUs
Measured throughput (tokens/s and requests/s), p50/p95/p99 latency and tail quantiles are reproducible within 5% between runs on the same pool configuration
Autoscaling policy hooks can be exercised by the harness and we can assert expected scale-up/scale-down behavior in controlled scenarios
End-to-end customer acceptance report is generated (PDF/HTML) that includes run artifact links, observed metrics, diffs from expected SLOs, and clear pass/fail verdicts
All runs are instrumented with tags (model, variant, seq_len_dist, batch_config, pool_id, run_id) that map back to Console dashboards and can be replayed by support/SEs
Security review signoff (if any sensitive trace sampling required) recorded in ticket comments
test_plan: Create a portable replay driver that consumes anonymized trace events (arrival_ts, prompt_len, model_hint, tenant_id) and emits requests against Dedicated endpoints
Implement deterministic pseudo-clock to ensure identical inter-request timing across runs and environments
Add KV-cache priming phase: replay warmup prefixes to populate caches and then run measurement windows
Support multiple spawn modes: single-tenant, multi-tenant mix, burst-ramp-sustain, and microburst emulation
Instrument autoscaler: tag traffic with policy stimuli and assert cluster size changes within expected time thresholds
Integrate with the metrics exporter to capture per-run token counts, GPU utilization, evictions, queueing, and scheduling latencies
Produce customer-facing artifact: template contains scenario description, run parameters, metric plots, and recommended tuning (batching, quantization, autoscale thresholds)
run_steps: 1) Prepare trace: use sanitized tenant trace or synthesized profile. Commit trace to artifacts bucket with run metadata
2) Provision test pool: spin up a reproducible Dedicated pool using infra-playbook (match size/GPU type/quant profile)
3) Warmup: run KV priming phase for configurable duration and verify cache hit rate > threshold
4) Measure: execute deterministic replay for the target duration, capturing system and application metrics
5) Autoscale test: drive sustained increase/decrease in offered load and validate scaler response windows
6) Teardown: collect logs, upload artifacts, and trigger post-processing to generate acceptance report
7) Signoff: attach report to customer onboarding ticket and run through checklist
instrumentation: Runner emits OpenTelemetry traces with attributes: run_id, pool_id, tenant_segment, model, seq_len_bucket
Prometheus exporter for per-GPU and per-pod metrics; Grafana dashboard template for the suite
Run artifacts stored in S3: raw request logs (anonymized), metrics dump (Prometheus snapshot), and scheduler trace samples
Console tags linking run_id to route/model-level dashboards for ad-hoc investigation
Synthetic golden-run baseline snapshots persisted for regression diffs
risks_and_tradeoffs: Synthetic replay can under/overestimate real tenant variance if traces are not representative; mitigation: include multiple tenant profiles and use a conservative margin in acceptance thresholds
Strong determinism requires infrastructure stability (identical kernel selection and GPU config); small infra drift may cause run variance — add snapshot/hash of runtime kernel versions to report
Autoscaler behavior in test can differ from production due to noise and background tenants; isolate test pool or use tenant-slice mode to reduce interference
Storing traces requires careful sanitization. If full fidelity captures prompt fragments, route through redaction pipeline and get security signoff
